feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 2 (body_length 0.20, wheel_track 0.09, y = 0.04, kp 2.5, kd 0.25) is the best raced result so far at 111.29. Oval progress was 0.53, max_error 0.0617 and steering_oscillation 0.246. Yaw inertia alone did not reduce oscillation much: 0.274 to 0.246 across iterations 1 to 2, and that change was confounded with the controller change. So the damping work now falls to the controller, and this candidate lowers kp to 2.2 and raises kd to 0.30. The sensor row move to y = 0.06 and body_length 0.22 are being tested for the first time. If the next race shows oval max_error below 0.06 and oscillation falling below about 0.2, keep the geometry and treat the s-bend and slalom exits as a bend-entry problem. If oval max_error is still at or above 0.06 while oscillation is below 0.2, move the outer sensors outward (requested change 1). If oscillation stays near 0.24 with max_error still near 0.06, the controller is the limit and geometry should stop chasing damping; hold body_length and try wheel_track (requested change 2). If line_loss_events rise above one per run on any track, the 16 mm footprints are overlapping too much (requested change 3).
requested_changes: If oval max_error is still at or above 0.06 while steering_oscillation is below 0.2: widen the outer sensors to x = plus or minus 0.05 m (sensor positions -0.05, -0.02, 0, 0.02, 0.05 at y = 0.06, sensor_size 0.016). Evidence: iteration 2 oval max_error 0.0617 with progress 0.53 shows the outer sensors still see the bend exit late, and iteration 1 showed the 16 mm outer sensors respond smoothly with no extra line loss.

If oval steering_oscillation stays near 0.24 after the controller change: keep body_length at 0.22 and do not add more yaw inertia; instead try wheel_track 0.085 m for more turn authority. Evidence: iteration 1 to 2 moved progress from 0.46 to 0.53 when wheel_track went from 0.10 to 0.09, and body_length 0.16 to 0.20 only moved oscillation from 0.274 to 0.246.

If line_loss_events rise above 1.0 per run on any track: return sensor_size to 0.012 and keep the outer sensors at x = plus or minus 0.04 m. Evidence: line_loss_events stayed at 0.9 to 1.0 in iterations 1 and 2 with 16 mm footprints, so any rise would indicate overlap near centre.
